newsitem.title: GERMANY: Two German insurers join forces in mega-merger.
newsitem.headline: Two German insurers join forces in mega-merger.

text.p: Two German insurers, Victoria Holding AG and Hamburg-Mannheimer AG, plan to merge to create the country's second largest insurer after Allianz AG, Victoria said late on Thursday.

The company's management boards signed a declaration of intent to link up in a bid to improve their position in Germany, the world's third-largest insurance market, and prepare for expansion across Europe, Victoria said in a mandatory statement released late on Thursday night.
The holding company for the new group will be called ERGO Versicherungsgruppe and will be based in Duesseldorf,
The group will have total premium income of 21 billion marks, investments exceeding 100 billion marks, and annual profit of 380 million marks based on combined 1996 results.

"The ERGO group will be excellently positioned in the German insurance market...with a good base for expanding business in the rest of Europe," Victoria said. It predicted above-average growth in premiums and results.
Reinsurance giant Munich Re , which owns 80 percent of Hamburg-Mannheimer as well as a minority stake in Victoria Holding, will hold a majority stake of ERGO based on preliminary valuations.

The move, which has yet to be approved by the German Federal Cartel Office and by shareholders, is part of a consolidation within Europe's insurance sector ahead of economic and monetary union, scheduled to start in 1999.
It follows the merger of UAP and Axa of France announced last November which ousted Allianz from the position of Europe's biggest insurer.

Munich Re said in a separate statement it supported the merger. Based on the accounts of the year 1996 alone, the link-up will result in an increase of around five marks in Munich Re's earnings per share.
The inclusion of Victoria in Munich Re's group of consolidated companies will boost Munich Re's consolidated premium income by some 8.4 billion marks to about 46.6 billion marks, Munich Re said.
Victoria Holding offers all the main lines of life and non-life insurance and owns D.A.S. Allgemeine Rechtsschutz-Versicherungs-AG, Europe's largest legal protection insurer, Victoria said.

The Hamburg-Mannheimer group, the second largest life insurer and the second largest personal accident insurer in Germany, also includes DKV Deutsche Krankenverischerung AG, Europe's largest private health insurer.
"It is envisaged that the group's business will focus primarily on personal lines insurance and commercial cover for small and medium-sized businesses," Victoria said.
The individual insurers will continue to operate with their established brand names.

Before the merger is effected, the stakes held by Hamburg-Mannheimer AG in the share capital of DKV Deutsche Krankenversicherung AG and Hamburg-Mannheimer Sachversicherungs-AG, currently amounting to nearly 40 percent each, are both to be increased to around 100 percent through capital increases in return for stock.
The values of Victoria and Hamburg-Mannheimer will be fixed in a legally prescribed procedure on the basis of valuations drawn up by auditing firms, Victoria said.
According to provisional valuations, this will produce a ratio of between 45:55 and 40:60, thereby giving Munich Re a majority interest in ERGO.
The valuations will be drawn up in October and general shareholder meetings are planned for November.
Edgar Jannott, management board chairman of Victoria is envisaged as chairman of ERGO, Victoria said.
Shares in ERGO will be listed on the stock exchanges of Frankfurt and Duesseldorf.
